correctness.rationale: Formal units B_j=A(x^{p^j}), R_j=B_j^p/B_{j+1} satisfy R_j in 1+p Z[[x]] by Freshman's dream. For U in 1+pZ[[x]], binomial induction U^{p^r} congruent 1 mod p^{r+1} works even for p=2. Exact telescoping A^{p^{2a}}/B_a^{p^a}=product_{j=0}^{a-1} R_j^{p^{2a-j-1}} therefore gives factorwise modulus p^{2a-j}, weakest p^{a+1}. Unit division by A preserves global coefficient congruence. At m=p^{a-1}, R_{a-1}=1-p x^m+ higher degrees; raising to p^a yields coefficient -p^{a+1}, all earlier R_j factors are congruent 1 mod p^{a+2}, and B_a^{p^a} starts only at degree p^a>m. Lower-degree residues vanish mod p^{a+2}, so division by A preserves nonzero sharp coefficient mod p^{a+2}. Supplied independent exact integer expansions check p=2,3,5,7 at low degrees; full theorem is analytic, not inferred from examples.
residual_risks: No non-prime-power extension claimed; no classification of every coefficient valuation.

originality.rationale: Sharma arXiv:2610.01422v1 explicitly proves coefficient congruence modulo p^a for t=p^a and its stronger p^2 only in special prime case a=1; the source itself asks about additional lifts. The present uniform a>=1 improvement and sharp witness address that open direction with a nontrivial new factorwise valuation. Han–Ono 2011 proves vanishing equivalence at t=3, not any general optimal p-adic modulus. A hidden classical lifting identity could imply it, so absolute priority is not asserted.
